answer: An agent market commissions renderings of an opal set against an umber dune. Agents earn queue slots by solving fresh hash puzzles. For each claim, the ledger hashes the round seed, agent key and submitted nonce, checks the result against a fixed target, and credits each valid proof once. There is no bonus for opening a new account. Ten slots require ten proofs, so an attacker needs roughly ten times the hashing work and energy to claim them, regardless of how many keys it creates.
